jurisdictions.name: Providence
jurisdictions.office: City of Providence Department of Inspection and Standards
notes: Providence publishes a Rhode Island Pool Barrier Checklist and says a permit is required for a pool or spa that can hold 24 inches or more of water.
The checklist says it incorporates the 2018 edition of the International Swimming Pool and Spa Code.
It lists a barrier at least 48 inches tall, no openings that pass a 4 inch sphere, a 36 inch clear zone around pumps and filters, and self-closing, self-latching gates that open away from the pool.
Under the zoning section it cites, no private pool or hot tub, including aprons and walks, may be in a front yard or a required corner or interior side setback.
The pool and its impervious apron count toward the rear yard and total impervious maximums.

sources.title: Rhode Island Pool Barrier Checklist (City of Providence), 10.21.25
Brochures, Applications and FAQ (City of Providence Inspection & Standards)

jurisdictions.name: Cranston
jurisdictions.office: Cranston Department of Building Inspections & Zoning
notes: The city's Building Inspection page says its department enforces the current edition of the Rhode Island State Building Code, the International Codes and the National Electrical Code as amended.
It says any contractor working on another person's home must be licensed or registered by the State of Rhode Island.
The department moved to 155 Gansett Avenue (rear) on March 23, 2026.

state_level.note: The Rhode Island Swimming Pool and Spa Code (510-RICR-00-00-14) adopts the 2021 edition of the International Swimming Pool and Spa Code, with state amendments.

source.title: Rhode Island Swimming Pool and Spa Code, 510-RICR-00-00-14 (RI Department of State)
